e2e-23191782-season-7686105.tracking: Registered here. The boundary is deliberate and published in three places — bilibili-asr-archive/README.md L301 ('feeds nothing below it'), docs/metadata-storage.md L288-305 ('the two paths do not feed each other yet'), and the iter-2026-09-bilibili-api-sqlite compass 'Out of scope' list — so this registers a known deferred capability, not a defect. Operator decision 2026-09-17: register only, no code change now ('只登记 residual，暂不动'). **2026-09-19 SURVEY CORRECTION (three registration errors, all verified at HEAD 887ef0e):** (1) the README anchor is **L333**, not L301 — the quoted sentence ('feeds nothing below it') is present, just 32 lines lower; docs/metadata-storage.md L288-305 is exact and its Boundary heading is real. (2) The queue attribution was wrong and is fixed in `scope`: `no-subtitle` lives in `acquisition_attempts.outcome` (schema-transcripts.sql:76) and surfaces through the `v_pending_subtitles` view (schema-transcripts.sql:106), read by `list_pending_subtitle_parts` / `count_pending_subtitle_parts` (database.py:1091/1125). `video_parts.processing_status` (models.py:15/24) cannot hold that value; only `_cmd_status` reads it (cli.py:1223). (3) 'documented non-goal of iter-2026-09-bilibili-api-sqlite' is only two-thirds true: that compass's Out-of-scope list excludes migration/import, audio download and ASR execution — it never names this bridge; the closest statement is its No-Migration Declaration. The title was softened accordingly. **Substance re-verified and unchanged:** all six ASR-chain handlers construct only `ManifestStore` (download-audio cli.py:1072-1099, asr :1696-1700, pilot :1974-1988, campaign :2266/2393-2400, run :2425-2433, schedule :2524-2553) with zero hits for archive.db/Database/Repository/storage across their spans; no ASR-chain module imports the storage layer; the only cross-store projection runs the OTHER way (cli.py:1280-1281, manifest to SQLite, used by status/runs); `storage/` contains no srt/txt/md reference at all. **Where the gap actually is (sizes the work honestly):** piece 1 (enumerate the audio queue from SQLite) has the SQL already but **no CLI wiring**; piece 2 (rebuild SRT/TXT/MD from stored transcripts) is **absent entirely** — the data is in `transcripts`/`transcript_segments`, `archive.write_archive` already renders segments to the three files, so what is missing is the command joining them plus a stem/version-identity decision (`list_transcript_versions`); piece 3 (give the legacy audio feeder a source) is confirmed absent (`needs_audio` is written only by subtitles.py:129 via _cmd_pilot, while harvest-subs goes through services.subtitle_ingest). **Cheapest corpus-unblocking slice is pieces 1+3, S-sized** (synthesize manifest rows `work_id = bvid:p{page}` from video_parts + v_pending_subtitles, or add `download-audio --from-sqlite`); the full three-piece closure is M-sized and should be staged. **2026-09-19 Phase-1 RECON — this row's own wording was wrong a second time and is now corrected in `scope`:** the earlier edit said v_pending_subtitles is "keyed on acquisition_attempts.outcome = 'no-subtitle'"; that string appears in NO SQL file. The view's predicate is absence of any transcript row plus processing_status <> 'gone' (schema-transcripts.sql:138-141), so never-attempted and failed parts are equally pending. A queue built from the old wording would have excluded precisely the fresh backlog it exists to serve. **What the recon established (all anchored, HEAD cf3f779):** (a) video_parts is the part identity (UNIQUE(bvid,page_index), surrogate video_part_id; cid stored but not unique) and work_id is COMPUTED in three separate views (schema.sql:128,159; schema-transcripts.sql:124) while Python computes the same form independently in page_identity.format_work_id — nothing enforces agreement. (b) transcripts.source_kind already allows 'asr-local' with a nullable model_id, and the partial content-uniqueness index explicitly leaves asr-local's per-model/run identity rule open with the comment that 'that decision belongs to the audio/ASR iteration' (schema-transcripts.sql:30-35) — an invitation this iteration should accept or explicitly decline. (c) acquisition_attempts.outcome is caption-only and its CHECK binds outcome to transcript_id/error_code, so per-part audio/ASR evidence has no home without a schema change; acquisition_runs.kind already accepts 'audio' and 'asr', so run-level rows need none. (d) The schema policy forbids migration: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cannot widen a constraint and an existing archive.db 'keeps the shape it has' (schema-transcripts.sql:4-10) — any widening applies to fresh databases only. (e) audio_objects / part_audio_objects / asr_models are declared-intentionally-empty scaffolding referenced by tests only, so a 'has audio' query over them runs clean and returns the whole corpus. (f) Rotation is a repository-level ORDER BY contract, not schema (database.py:1091-1123, 'the locked contract the CLI reads'), and it depends on per-part attempt evidence audio cannot currently record — a naive 'no audio row' queue has no recency column and would re-attempt the same head every bounded run. (g) The NOT EXISTS in v_pending_subtitles has no source_kind filter, so writing an asr-local transcript silently drains the subtitle backlog and changes what count_pending_subtitle_parts means. (h) v_pending_metadata is a second, unrelated 'pending' notion one function name away (MetadataRepository.list_pending_parts = metadata NOT yet collected) and the CLI's only backlog line already prints it under the bare label 'pending:' — a naming trap a plan must avoid. (i) On the manifest side, needs_audio's only writer was the legacy harvest path that harvest-subs bypassed, no code sets pending/meta_ok/sub_checked, and upsert rejects a new row without a page-qualified work_id — so no code path can birth a manifest row today. (j) The ASR chain reads subtitle segments from the FILESYSTEM (subtitles/raw/{stem}.json), not from transcript_segments, so a synthesized subtitle_done row would reach the archive stage and skip with missing_subtitle_raw. (k) duration_s (not duration_ms) is load-bearing for the audio budget and fails closed: a row without a converted duration skips every download. e2e-23191782-season-7686105.source: Deep text-quality pass over the season run's 14 archives, 2026-09-17 ({WORKFLOW_DIR}/e2e-23191782-season-7686105/reports/e2e.md, text-quality section). e2e-23191782-season-7686105.scope: bilibili-asr-archive/src/bili_asr/asr.py _token_cues: `parts.append(piece)` + `text = _clean_text(pending + "".join(parts))` versus `_join_text`, which is called only from `hand_back()` and from the undersized-cue absorption path. `_join_text`'s own docstring already declares the phenomenon and the rule ('Nano emits an English phrase as several tokens and does not always carry the leading space'), so this is the rule applied in two of the three places it is needed. Chinese text is unaffected, which is why 13 of 14 items show none.
e2e-23191782-season-7686105.target: the next attempt must FIRST obtain the material this rule needs. **Corrected 2026-09-19:** the blocker is not 'the evidence is gone' but 'no code path retains it'. The archived payload cannot carry it by construction — both ASR write sites pass `raw=None` (cli.py:1791-1793 in the `asr` branch, cli.py:1922-1924 in `_cmd_pilot`), so archive.py:481-484 synthesizes the `segments`/`source`/`provenance` shape — and the model result is already gone before that (`ASRRunner.transcribe` returns `normalize_result(result)`, asr.py:611-641 to 823-846). 20260918-operational-record-coverage.title: The interruption record is preserved across the whole coordinator unwind, but **not** universally: a second `SIGINT` landing inside the run body's `except KeyboardInterrupt` clause *after* the exception match and *before* the ignore pair is installed leaves `interrupted`/`exit_code` still `None`, so the `finally` fails all three guards and writes no record — the exit is then a propagating `KeyboardInterrupt` (a subprocess probe returns -2 — signal-killed with a traceback — so a shell still reports 130, but it is not the run body's own `return 128 + 2`).
20260918-operational-record-coverage.source: Plan QC targeted re-review of 20260918-operational-record-coverage, 2026-09-18 — qc2.md wave-2 round (disclosure (a), `accepted-limitation`), with two corrections the seat required in the register text: the guarantee is not universal, and the cost of closing it is lower than the fix wave claimed.
20260918-operational-record-coverage.scope: bilibili-asr-archive/src/bili_asr/cli.py — the run body's `except KeyboardInterrupt` clause (the window between the clause matching and `_ignore_interruption_signals()`), and the `finally`'s three guards that decide whether a record is written. The unwind *outside* that clause is safe: a second Ctrl-C there is caught by the same clause, the record is still written exactly once and the exit is still 130.
20260918-operational-record-coverage.target: a plan that owns the interruption contract's remaining window. Closing it needs a SIGINT disposition rather than a statement-order change (the guard is already the clause's first statement): install a handler that calls `_ignore_interruption_signals()` and then delegates to `signal.default_int_handler`, which keeps `KeyboardInterrupt` semantics for inner frames — note qc2's correction that the earlier framing ("a custom handler would change KeyboardInterrupt semantics for every inner frame") overstated the cost; what any handler-based fix does change is one-shot SIGINT for the rest of the run, already accepted for SIGTERM.
20260918-operational-record-coverage.tracking: Registered here at the plan's QC gate (2026-09-18). Measured exposure: a few bytecodes wide with no calls in it (nanoseconds), and standard signals coalesce while the first is still unprocessed, so a human double-press (milliseconds apart) lands in the safe unwind, not in this window. Latent, not live — but not zero, and it is the same record-loss mode the plan exists to remove, which is why it is registered rather than absorbed. Sibling rows: R2 (process start → the guard), R1 (`schedule`/`campaign`). Sibling limitation carried in the same row, registered 2026-09-18 after the QA gate pointed out it had no durable carrier: `signal.getsignal(SIGINT)` returns `None` for a disposition not installed from Python, and `signal.signal(sig, None)` raises, so that case cannot be restored — QC judged it an `accepted-limitation` (unreachable on the supported entry path: CPython installs `default_int_handler` for SIGINT at startup and nothing in this path replaces it; and bounded, because the restore runs *after* the record is written, so the worst case is a traceback instead of a clean 130, not data loss). The same pattern already existed for `SIGTERM`. No guard was added, deliberately. **2026-09-19 SURVEY VERIFICATION:** claim still true, with one correction now applied to `scope`. The clause is cli.py:2480-2489: `except KeyboardInterrupt:` at :2480, comment lines :2481-2486, and `_ignore_interruption_signals()` as the clause's first STATEMENT at :2487 (comments are not bytecode, so the surviving window is exactly the exception match to that call: a LOAD_GLOBAL and the call, no intervening statement and no intervening call). The finally's three guards are :2499 `if interrupted is not None:`, :2506 `elif exit_code is not None:`, :2509 `if exit_code is not None:` — with both state variables None (:2452-2453) the write is skipped and the finally completes having written nothing. The width claim is honest. The prescribed disposition (a handler that installs the ignores then delegates to `signal.default_int_handler`) is accurate and does preserve `KeyboardInterrupt` for inner frames — what it changes is one-shot SIGINT for the remainder of the run, and it must be paired with the existing capture/restore at cli.py:2363/:2367 so the true previous disposition still returns after the write. **Exit-code correction:** a bare propagating `KeyboardInterrupt` measured as subprocess returncode **-2** (CPython re-raises SIGINT to itself after printing the traceback), so the shell still sees 130 — the observable difference is the traceback and the lost `SystemExit`, not the numeric status. A future implementer should not test for a 130-versus-signal distinction the shell cannot see.

iter-2026-09-artifact-root.title: The artifact-root configuration's operational hardening is missing: the cap/peak measurement re-based onto the artifact root **walks the whole `audio/` tree once or twice per row** (a network round trip on the intended WebDAV mount), the same measurement **fails open** (an unreadable/absent mount yields 0 bytes, silently disabling the cumulative guard and printing the 0 as evidence), and the boundary's validation **opens** the root but never probes a write or a directory `fsync`, so a mount that opens and then rejects directory fsync passes validation and fails every row with a raw error instead of the four-line refusal.

Not a defect of the delivered split: state still stays local and the refusal ordering holds. **Close condition must enumerate all four items** (the per-row walk cost, the fail-open measurement, the write+directory-fsync probe, and qc3's Suggestion S1 - a fixture for each), **plus** qualifying the unqualified `fail-closed` claims - `docs/artifact-root.md:141` (done in fix wave 2) **and the two siblings the wave did not reach, `docs/audio-retention-policy.md:39` and `:179`** (qc3's re-review finding), **plus** qc3's S2 (probe budget multiplied by the base count in per-row loops) and S3 (one `schedule --allow-long-live` run measures usage twice by different recipes, so the printed plan can disagree with the batch's own skip), which the QC re-review found unregistered.
iter-2026-09-artifact-root.target: a plan that owns the operator's network-mount configuration end to end: sample the peak only where it is read (one snapshot per batch), distinguish "measured empty" from "cannot measure" (fail-closed), and add a write+fsync probe (or declare fsync-hostile mounts out of contract). Trigger: the first real corpus run with `--artifact-root` on the WebDAV mount, or any plan touching `audio_budget.py`'s call sites. **FIX DESIGN (PM, 2026-09-20 — written so the next Prepare starts from a spec, not a diagnosis): (1) the usage measurement must stop returning a bare int — `audio_dir_usage_bytes` returns a result that carries either a measured byte count or an explicit unmeasurable reason, so 'the mount could not be read' cannot be silently rendered as 0; (2) the cumulative guard fails CLOSED on unmeasurable: the run is refused through the existing four-line refusal surface instead of proceeding with a fabricated 0, and the printed usage line says 'cannot measure (<reason>)'; (3) the peak/usage sample moves from per-row to once per batch, so the failure point collapses into startup rather than depending on the mount being readable at every row (measured cost makes this a correctness change, not a performance one: 0.39 ms empty -> 0.97 ms @200 files); (4) the artifact-root boundary validation gains ONE startup probe — create-temp / fsync(file) / fsync(dir) / unlink — refusing with a named line when the mount rejects it, with 'declare fsync-hostile mounts out of contract' as the documented fallback if the probe proves unusable. Verification: a fixture whose `audio/` is absent / a dangling symlink / a non-directory must produce the REFUSAL (the negative control this repo's absence-assertion rule requires), a genuinely empty tree must still read 0, and the fsync rejection is pinned with a faked fd layer rather than a real hostile mount.

iter-2026-09-artifact-root.scope: `artifact_root.py`'s value object and every reader/writer call site that pairs a recorded value with a base. **A fourth specific (disclosed by the fix wave and CORRECTED by both re-review seats, 2026-09-19):** the holding-base rule in `_audio_base_holding`/`_declared_audio`/`_audio_base_for_path` picks by **existence**, while the two `_existing_audio` helpers require a usable size (`st_size > 0`). **The consequence is NOT a failed row** - both seats probed it: a 0-byte stub at the configured root is skipped by the producer, the valid legacy copy is returned, and on the recorded branch the row simply falls through to the (now corrected) download branch. What the divergence actually costs today is **one extra download-stage fast-path call**. The rule still matters because a future existence-only call site could reintroduce the difference - so the shared resolver should fold **validity** (existence *and* a usable size) into the base choice. *(The earlier text in this row said the stub makes the row fail closed; that was the PM's inference, not a measurement, and two seats disproved it - the same claim-wider-than-the-code class this iteration keeps catching.)* **Also: the enumeration is stale by one** - `cli._audio_base_for_path` (added by fix wave 2) is a **fifth** pairing site, and qc3's S4 (the download branch validates the same absolute path twice and re-derives its relative form where the coordinator's sibling returns the pair in one pass, with a mount flap between the two probes surfacing as the same `invalid audio path` refusal) sits inside this row's scope and needs no separate entry.
iter-2026-09-artifact-root.target: a plan that adds a third artifact family or a second configurable root, or any refactor pass over `artifact_root.py`: promote one resolver (e.g. `resolve_audio_holder(roots, declared) -> tuple[Path, str] | None`) into the module and route the audio sites through it, so a new family contributes a guard rather than a fifth loop. Trigger: the next artifact family, or the next time two same-named helpers drift.
iter-2026-09-artifact-root.tracking: Registered at this plan's QC gate (2026-09-19). The Critical it caused is fixed in the fix wave with the minimal change; this row exists so the *shape* that allowed it is not lost when the fix looks sufficient. **Three specifics the QC re-review requires in this row so a future resolver actually closes it** (qc-specialist-2): (i) today the cross-base download route *self-heals* only because `audio._mark_audio_ok` writes `status=audio_ok` and the correctly base-resolved `audio_path` **before** the pilot raises - a resolver that moves that write turns the route into a permanent failure; (ii) the second entry point is a `meta_ok` row flipped to `needs_audio` by `harvest_subtitle` while a legacy copy sits at the archive root, so the fix belongs in the shared resolver and not in a status predicate; (iii) the operator-facing line is `archive failed: invalid audio path`, **not** one of the four refusal lines, which makes it easy to mistake for a data problem. e2e-23191782-longform-pair-webdav.title: A part that already carries an **AI caption** cannot be put through the audio→ASR branch at all: `derive-manifest` excludes it by design (the queue is 'no transcript'), and no shipping flag overrides that, so a local ASR transcript cannot be produced for a captioned item — and the audio branch of the two most recent iterations stays unverified on a live row.

The executor verified there is no back door: `_todo_for_bvid` returns `[]` and `write_archive` has no transcript-reading call site.
e2e-23191782-longform-pair-webdav.scope: The audio/ASR selection surface (`download-audio --missing-subs`, `asr --pending`, `run --scope pending`, `derive-manifest`'s predicate) for parts that hold a stored transcript. Not a defect of the cap: 'subtitles first, local ASR as fallback' is the published design and every command behaved as documented. What is unverified because of it: the artifact-root product placement (`/mnt/123pan`) on a real archived row, and the audio→ASR path of `iter-2026-09-artifact-root` / `iter-2026-09-queue-bridge` on live data. The 2026-09-17 season run remains the only live audio evidence and predates both iterations.
e2e-23191782-longform-pair-webdav.target: **Route B first (PM decision 2026-09-20): verify the audio branch with NO product change** — pick items that genuinely lack captions (the branch-deciding probe is `probe-subs` over candidate parts, run at scope-lock time, never inherited from a stored manifest) and run them through download-audio -> GPU ASR -> product placement on the artifact root. **Route A (deferred, needs evidence before it ships): an explicit override that widens the SELECTOR, never the queue predicate** — `derive-manifest`'s `v_pending_subtitles` criterion stays byte-identical; only an operator naming a part explicitly may select a caption-bearing one, and the manifest row/provenance must record that the local ASR was forced (otherwise no later reader can explain why that row carries a local transcript). Name it through the naming-analyzer skill if it ever ships. Rationale for the order: no current operator need demonstrates 'I want local ASR for a captioned lecture', and widening the CLI surface on speculation is the class this repository keeps paying for. Original row target follows. the next planning round that decides whether the audio branch needs a live re-verification: either an explicit opt-in to run ASR for caption-bearing parts (a product decision with its own scope), or an E2E over items that genuinely lack captions. Closing condition: a live archived row produced through the audio branch on the current build, OR a recorded decision that the branch is covered by the 2026-09-17 evidence and needs no re-verification.

e2e-23191782-longform-pair-webdav.target: the next plan that touches `fetch-meta`'s page loop (or the scheduler that calls it). Candidate closers: a bounded retry/backoff with the same exit taxonomy, an explicit skip-past-blocked-page option, or a documented operator recipe. e2e-23191782-longform-pair-webdav.tracking: Registered 2026-09-20 at the E2E workflow's close. Immediate operator workaround available today: `fetch-meta --start-page 4` steps over the blocked page, and the cursor makes the stop resumable. 20260922-target-host-reconciliation.title: The root registry is versioned while the documents it points at are not: `.mstar/status.json` is tracked in git, `.mstar/workflows/**` is gitignored, so a workflow registration (and its `dir`) reaches a checkout whose snapshot document never travelled — that checkout then holds a live registry row naming a directory that does not exist.
20260922-target-host-reconciliation.source: Measured on the target host (192.168.3.21 WSL) 2026-09-22 while reconciling its checkout. `git ls-files .mstar/status.json` -> tracked; `.gitignore:1-7` ignores `.mstar/**` except `AGENTS.md`, `knowledge/`, `specs/`. The host's only registered row was `e2e-23191782-longform-pair-webdav` with `dir: workflows/e2e-23191782-longform-pair-webdav`, and `find .mstar -maxdepth 3 -iname "*e2e*"` returned nothing. The registration was authored at `f85fe91` (which the host had) while the snapshot document is untracked, so it never arrived. Cleared on that host by the fast-forward to `37b0acc`, whose committed `status.json` carries `workflows: []`.
20260922-target-host-reconciliation.scope: The harness's cross-clone boundary for the root registry. `mstar-artifacts` states the default policy verbatim: the clone handoff surface is tracked `{HARNESS_DIR}/AGENTS.md`, `{KNOWLEDGE_DIR}/**`, `{SPECS_DIR}/**` and root `CONCEPTS.md` / `STRATEGY.md`, and `status.json` / `workflows/` are explicitly NOT that surface. This repository force-added `status.json`, so one half of a two-document lifecycle is versioned and the other half is not. Consequence observed: the registry row is read by the engine while its `dir` is absent, so the lifecycle it describes cannot be inspected from that checkout at all. Two candidate closers: (a) untrack `status.json` (`git rm --cached .mstar/status.json`) so both halves stay machine-local runtime state, or (b) track the snapshot directory too, so a registration always arrives with its document. Either way the closing condition needs one check that every row in the registry resolves to an existing directory in the checkout that reads it.
20260922-target-host-reconciliation.target: The next harness-maintenance round that touches `.gitignore` or the harness tracking policy. Closing condition: one of the two closers above, plus a registry check that a row's `dir` exists.

20260922-proofread-wave.title: **The ASR hotword list is also an insertion source.** A token from the run's own `provenance.hotwords` is written into the transcript where the speaker said something else — measured in **6 of 6** proofread items, including **two cases where the transcriber/corrector completed the hotword phrase with a character that appears in neither source**. The project's own hotword scoring counts *surface occurrences*, so it cannot separate a recovered term from an inserted one: the corpus-wide count that made the ASR look like the stronger system on domain vocabulary is contaminated.
20260922-proofread-wave.source: Proofreading wave, 2026-09-22 (six items, 7.30 h of audio, UID 23191782; each item read against both machine transcripts by an independent seat and then audited by a second, independent seat). Decisive criterion used throughout: the token is in the run's `provenance.hotwords` **and** the live AI caption over the same span is unrelated text **and** the ASR confidence there is low. Measured instances: `国际劳工仲裁` **13× on ASR sides vs 0× on any caption side** across the six items (e.g. ASR「但是国际劳工仲裁，它和一个东西没有关系」vs caption「但是所有人哈姆拉加起来他和一个东西没有关系」); `未明子` ≥9× (replacing 为你 / 我也知道 / 或者说); `马恩牌` 3× (replacing the deliberate character-split joke 马叉虫); `齐泽克` (replacing 骑在头上), `黑格尔`, `主义主义`, `根正苗红`, and the English string `International Employment Matters Tribunal`. Fabrications (a character present in neither source, added to complete a hotword): `BV1vNTqzFEve 00:05:55` ASR「就这么正苗红」+ caption「就这么这么简单」→ shipped 「就这么**根正苗红**」; and `BV1BdtazGEBE 00:15:50` (same class, caught only by the repair seat's own sweep). Negative control that keeps this honest: `拉康`/`辩证法`/`此在`/`实存` in the same list are **caption-attested** at their spans and were correctly kept — a hotword hit is not automatically an insertion. Reporting detail: the E2E's own hotword figure ("ASR 2–17 hits per item vs caption 0–3") counted occurrences, which is why it read as a win; the corrected statement is that an unknown share of those hits are insertions.
20260922-proofread-wave.scope: The decoder's hotword prior and every consumer of it, including the project's own measurement of the feature. Two legs: (a) **the transcript product** — an operator reading an archived transcript cannot tell a spoken term from an injected one, which is the archive's core value proposition; (b) **the measurement** — `hotword-list-measurement.md`'s family of measurements scores a hotword by its presence in the output, so a hotword that raises the score by hallucinating counts the same as one that raises it by correcting. Closers for (a): ship the hotword list as a *soft* prior with an insertion guard (e.g. require the token to survive a second decode, or gate it on the caption when a caption exists), or record per-token provenance so a consumer can see which terms came from the prior; for (b): score with a **caption-conditioned** or insertion-penalised metric that separates recovery from injection, and re-measure the existing shard results under it. Closing condition: one of those lands and the corpus-level measurement is restated with insertions counted separately.
20260922-proofread-wave.target: The next iteration or plan that touches the ASR hotword configuration, `src/bili_asr/asr.py`'s hotword handling, or the hotword measurement family in `{KNOWLEDGE_DIR}`. Closing condition: a measurement that separates recovery from insertion exists and is applied to the six-item corpus, and the product either guards the insertion path or documents per-token provenance.

20260922-proofread-wave.title: **A source-reducing formatting step was not count-guarded, and it silently narrowed what six reviewers could see.** The alignment table I built for the proofreading wave assigned each caption cue to an ASR-derived time block by its **midpoint**; a cue whose midpoint fell between blocks (i.e. inside an ASR VAD gap) belonged to no block and was **dropped from the table entirely** — 251 of 9607 cues (2.6%), with no `⟨空缺⟩` marker and no count check.
20260922-proofread-wave.source: Measured 2026-09-22 during and after the proofreading wave. Root cause: `blocks()` derives block spans from ASR segments only, and each caption cue is attached by `block.start <= cue_midpoint < block.end`; a cue in a VAD gap matches no block. Corpus result: 251/9607 cues dropped (BV1BdtazGEBE 66, BV1iddQYQE7D 82, BV1vNTqzFEve 56, BV1Y7M4zNEfF 21, BV1zz5zzFENq 15, BV11p5qzAE6s 11). Independent confirmation: the reviewer for `BV1zz5zzFENq` reported, without knowing the cause, that the caption column was “a lossier capture than the raw caption JSON at the same publish path — 15 clause-drops / 186 chars” — exactly my measurement for that item. **Only after the repair seats worked the lists item by item did the real content cost become measurable: 13 short utterances added (BV1BdtazGEBE 3, BV1iddQYQE7D 6, BV1vNTqzFEve 2, BV1zz5zzFENq 1, others 0) plus 1 marked**; the remaining dropped cues were carried by adjacent ASR segments that were in the table. My first estimate (100 cues “missing from both”) was an upper bound from a substring test and was wrong by roughly an order of magnitude — the corrected figure is the 13 above.
20260922-proofread-wave.scope: Verification methodology, not product code: any transformation that sits **between a source and the person or agent judging it** and can lose source text without saying so. This instance was ad-hoc tooling for one E2E, so the durable form of the lesson is a rule, not a patch: a source-reducing step must (a) account for every input item (count in == count out, with an explicit bucket for “not attached”), (b) never render a dropped item as silence. It sits in the same family as `{KNOWLEDGE_DIR}/best-practices/premise-freshness-before-lock.md` (a premise inherited rather than re-verified) and the E2E's own `absence-assertion-negative-control` discipline. Closers: record the rule where the project's verification methodology lives (a best-practice note or the E2E contract), or nothing — accepted as a closed one-off with the measurement above as its record.
20260922-proofread-wave.target: The next iteration close (`mstar-compound`) that promotes verification lessons, or the next E2E that builds an alignment table between two sources. Closing condition: the count-guard rule is recorded, or a recorded decision that it is not worth promoting.

The repair wave closed the gap: each item now carries a `## 本次修复 · 丢弃字幕条清点` table with every dropped cue's disposition (`已在` / `补入` / `标记`). Graded `low` on consequence (13 short utterances in a byproduct, all now either carried or added) and **not** low on lesson (a silent loss on the evidence path is exactly the class this project keeps paying for).

20260925-archive-db-review.title: A dead `SESSDATA` makes the caption channel return an empty inventory, and that emptiness is recorded as `no-subtitle` — a durable false negative that `credential_present` cannot flag, because it records presence, not validity.
20260925-archive-db-review.source: Ad-hoc `archive.db` / gateway review, 2026-09-25. Two probes. (a) 40 videos sampled at random from the 1730-video `recArchivesByKeywords` enumeration: `get_video_parts` -> first `cid` -> `get_subtitle_tracks` returned **0/40** with any track and 0 errors. (b) The 6 parts the store itself holds `subtitle-ai` transcripts for (acquired 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-12) re-probed with the same credential: **0/6** tracks, and identically **0/6** anonymously. `/x/web-interface/nav` returns `code=-101`, `isLogin=false`, both with the `.env` cookie and without it. Probe (b) contradicts a recorded positive, so the empty result is a credential/visibility artifact and not evidence about caption availability; the two readings are not separable on the current surface.
20260925-archive-db-review.scope: `src/bili_asr/services/subtitle_ingest.py`'s outcome mapping (an empty track inventory maps to `no-subtitle`, never to `failed`) together with the evidence column that mapping writes, `acquisition_runs.credential_present` (`storage/schema-transcripts.sql`), and the rule `{KNOWLEDGE_DIR}/architecture-patterns/subtitle-acquisition-contract.md` states: login-gated tracks 'become visible through the credential in effect (the SESSDATA cookie), not through a request flag'. A present-but-expired credential is stored as `credential_present=1` beside `outcome='no-subtitle'` — the one combination a later reader would take as 'an authenticated probe found nothing'. Nothing under `src/` probes validity: `NAV_URL` is used only to fetch the WBI key pair (`bili_client.py:394-404`), and it actively tolerates the logged-out answer through `accept_codes={-101}`. Consequence: the caption backlog can fill with false negatives that rotate to the back of `v_pending_subtitles` indefinitely, each indistinguishable from a genuinely caption-less part.
20260925-archive-db-review.target: The next session that resumes the caption path, before any `harvest-subs` / `probe-subs` invocation against the live corpus. Closing condition: the credential's validity is established one way or the other (re-login and re-probe the six known positives, or an explicit decision that the account is unavailable), and the outcome mapping either separates an unusable credential from a genuinely empty inventory or the ledger says which of the two readings applies.

20260925-archive-db-review.title: `video_parts.processing_status` carries an unreachable state (`metadata_collected`), so `v_pending_metadata` and the `status` command's `pending:` line report a backlog that can never shrink.
20260925-archive-db-review.source: Ad-hoc `archive.db` review, 2026-09-25, against the real store `.tmp/e2e-23191782/archive/archive.db`. 63 parts, all `processing_status='discovered'`, every one of them already carrying `cid`, `title` and `duration_ms`; 6 of them additionally hold a stored transcript. `v_pending_metadata` returns 63 while `v_pending_subtitles` returns 57, and the 6-part difference is exactly the parts that already have a transcript — so the two views disagree about whether those parts are pending anything. Whole-repo grep for a writer of `metadata_collected` outside tests, `Literal` declarations and schema text: none. The single writer is `services/metadata_ingest.py:426`, which hardcodes `processing_status='discovered'` inside the same transaction that writes `cid`/`title`/`duration_ms`, so metadata is collected at the moment of discovery and no later pass ever advances the state.
20260925-archive-db-review.scope: `storage/schema.sql`'s `video_parts.processing_status` domain (`discovered` | `metadata_collected` | `gone`) and the view that reads it, `v_pending_metadata` (`schema.sql:156`), surfaced by `status` as `pending:` (`cli.py:1684-1690` via `list_pending_parts`, `storage/database.py:659`); `docs/metadata-storage.md:80` documents that view as 'the `status` command's pending work'. Only `discovered`, and per the knowledge base `gone`, are meaningful in practice, so `pending:` is a constant equal to the part count. This is not a wrong-action bug: `derive-manifest` deliberately reads the other queue (`v_pending_subtitles` through `list_pending_subtitle_parts`) and `cli.py:1209-1211` documents that separation, so no command acts on the misleading number. It is a false operator signal whose fix is a design choice rather than a patch: (a) write `metadata_collected` from a real second pass, (b) redefine `v_pending_metadata` to read the condition it actually means, or (c) drop the state and the view.
20260925-archive-db-review.target: The next plan that touches `video_parts`' status column, `v_pending_metadata`, or the `status` command's output. Closing condition: `pending:` either names a work set that can shrink or is removed, and the `processing_status` domain has no unreachable member.

20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers.title: **The merged ASR boundary could not read the audio the archive's own downloader writes.** `transcribe()` read every input with `soundfile`, and libsndfile reads WAV/FLAC/OGG/MP3 but not **AAC** — which is the codec inside the `.m4a` container `cli.py:1574` / `audio.py` produce for the preferred DASH audio stream. So `bili-asr asr` failed on its own product's audio with `archive failed (OSError)` and archived nothing, and the failure was invisible to the 2026-09-24 end-to-end measurement because that measurement ran on a PCM `.wav`.
20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers.source: Found 2026-09-25 while preparing the T5 hotword measurement, reproduced on the target host (`chosenecho@192.168.3.21` WSL, RX 7800 XT gfx1101). (a) `sf.read` on a real corpus `.m4a` raises `soundfile.LibsndfileError: Error opening …: Format not recognised`; `soundfile.available_formats()` lists `MP3` and no AAC/M4A entry, libsndfile 1.2.2. (b) The same audio transcoded losslessly to FLAC archives normally: `1 archived`, `asr_hotwords` 26 entries read back. (c) `sf.read` on the 2026-09-24 measurement input `/tmp/full_item.wav` (pcm_s16le, 2843 s) succeeds — that is why the earlier run was green. (d) The test fixtures are `.wav` throughout, and the only `.m4a`-named test wrote a `b"payload"` blob and never decoded it. (e) The retired FunASR engine did not have this gap: its VAD component shelled out to `ffmpeg` (`_materialize_input`'s own docstring says so), so `.m4a` worked; the transformers rewrite moved decoding in-process and lost it. `plan §13.1` had flagged `_materialize_input` as 'verify before deleting' and the verification was never run.
20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers.scope: `bilibili-asr-archive/src/bili_asr/asr.py`'s audio-read step, and every consumer of it: the `asr`/`run`/`pilot` CLI paths, `coordinator` batches, and the T5 measurement itself. The gap is about **the product reading its own storage format**, not about one codec: `path_policy.AUDIO_EXTENSIONS` admits exactly `.m4a` and `.flac`, so one of the two admitted extensions was unreadable for the one codec it normally holds. Closing condition: an `.m4a`/AAC row transcribes through the CLI on the target host, a test fails if the reader narrows again, and the reader dependency is stated where an operator installs the `[asr]` extra.
20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers.target: Closed inside iteration `iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout`, plan `20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers`, on the same round that found it — the measurement could not proceed on real audio otherwise.
20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers.tracking:
Fixed 2026-09-26 in commit `0a95035` (worktree `.worktrees/20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers`, branch `feat/20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers`): `_read_audio()` keeps `soundfile` as the primary reader and falls back to `librosa` on `LibsndfileError`. `librosa` was already a declared `[asr]` dependency (`pyproject.toml`) and already imported by this module for resampling, so no dependency was added. Decode fidelity was measured before trusting it: `librosa.load` of a corpus `.m4a` against `ffmpeg -ar 48000 -ac 2` of the same file gives zero length difference and maximum absolute difference `0.000000`. Verified end to end on the target host — `BV1wLTP6NE9h:p0` (448 s, AAC): `archived (asr)`, and `BV1zz5zzFENq:p0` before it. Four tests in `tests/test_asr_qwen.py` pin the boundary; three of them fail with the fix reverted (`AttributeError: module 'bili_asr.asr' has no attribute '_read_audio'`), and `tests/test_asr_qwen.py` is 40 passed on the host. The tests' autouse torch stand-in gained a `Tensor` class in the same commit: `scipy` probes for it through `librosa`'s resampler, and the missing attribute made a test fail for a reason unrelated to the code under test. What is **not** closed by this row: the reason the original suite could not have caught it — every ASR fixture is `.wav`, so no test ever decoded the container the downloader writes. A fixture that round-trips a real `.m4a` is owed to the next round that touches this suite.

 **The fallback's own chain, observed on the target host 2026-09-26 while the short corpus ran** (the warning `PySoundFile failed. Trying audioread instead.` appears once per `.m4a`): `librosa.load` does not decode AAC itself — it falls through to **`audioread`**, whose `FFmpegAudioFile` backend drives the system `ffmpeg` 6.1.1, reported as channels=2 samplerate=48000 for a corpus file. This is guaranteed rather than incidental: `audioread>=2.1.9` is a *hard* dependency of `librosa` (verified with `importlib.metadata.requires('librosa')`), and `ffmpeg` is already required by the product (`AGENTS.md`). So the repair does not add a dependency, but it does mean **`ffmpeg` is on the decode path for AAC regardless of which reader is primary** — the same program the retired FunASR-era VAD shelled out to, now reached through a library instead of directly. Worth stating plainly because it bounds what the repair can promise: an environment with `librosa` but no `ffmpeg` would still fail on `.m4a`, and `pyproject.toml` lists only the Python side.
20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers.closure_evidence: Commits `0a95035` (first repair) and `f4c0ebb` (the repair that holds). Fix plan for the second: `.mstar/plans/audit-2026-09-26/001-fix-aac-decode-contract.md` (tasks 3 and 7). The fixture that was owed, now in the suite: `bilibili-asr-archive/tests/test_asr_qwen.py` — `_write_aac()` (ffmpeg-generated, skips where ffmpeg is absent, so no media enters the repo) plus `test_a_real_aac_file_is_decoded_through_the_fallback`. Mutation-verified on chosenecho@192.168.3.21: neutralising the fallback fails it along with 2 others; restored, the ASR suite is 44 passed. Clean-venv verification with **no librosa**: generated AAC -> (89088,)@44100, and the real corpus `BV1zz5zzFENq.p0.m4a` -> (100167680, 2)@48000. The README's decode section was corrected in the same commit, since the previous text described the librosa/audioread chain this row's first fix depended on.
20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers.closure_note: Closed on the second attempt, and the row is worth reading in that order. The defect (the boundary could not read the `.m4a` its own downloader writes) was fixed in `0a95035`, but that fix routed the fallback through `librosa.load` and did not survive independent review: `librosa` 1.0 dropped `audioread`, so on a host built from this repo's own declarations the fallback re-raised the very `LibsndfileError` it existed to catch — registered as `iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout · R5` and now closed too. Commit `f4c0ebb` replaces it with the `ffmpeg` binary and `soxr`. This row's own owed follow-up — "a fixture that round-trips a real `.m4a` is owed to the next round that touches this suite" — is discharged by that commit: `test_a_real_aac_file_is_decoded_through_the_fallback` encodes AAC with ffmpeg at test time and decodes it, and it fails when the fallback is neutralised.

20260924-qwen3-asr-transformers.source: Self-inflicted, found 2026-09-26 by the operator's own re-seed. iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.closure_note: Fixed in commit f4c0ebb (branch feat/20260927-aac-decode-contract, plan 20260927-aac-decode-contract), not by pinning librosa but by removing it from the decode path entirely: the fallback is now the `ffmpeg` binary the product already requires (audio.py:71 already shells to it; AGENTS.md declares it), and resampling moved to `soxr`, which is exactly what `librosa.resample` calls at its default `res_type="soxr_hq"` and which the corpus measured bit-identical. The `[asr]` extra no longer contains librosa, so the version range that caused this cannot recur. The guard now covers `soxr` too, so a partial extra reports through ASRDependencyError. This also closes the larger risk the row's title understated: librosa 1.0.0 requires numpy>=2.1.0 while the verified ROCm recipe runs numpy 1.26.4, so the unbounded extra would have dragged a numpy major version into a verified GPU environment — worth recording, because the next person tempted by `librosa>=0.10` should know it is not only an AAC problem. What the closure does NOT claim: nothing was re-measured on a GPU; the decode and resample paths were verified on the target host and in a clean venv, and the ASR transcription itself is the pre-existing, already-verified behaviour. Two further defects were found in this fix by an independent adversarial read and fixed before the branch was considered done — the ffmpeg child inheriting stdin (a piped `q` aborted a valid decode) and the WAVE muxer silently truncating past 4 GiB with ffmpeg still exiting 0, which is a live risk for items over ~3.1 h. Both are reproduced and mutation-tested in `d4f57cb`. Reviewed again after this closure, as a whole-branch adversarial pass: three seats covered runtime code, tests and documentation. Two of their findings were coverage holes in this fix's own tests (a primary read that no longer had a round-trip; `AudioDecodeError` reaching no test at all) and one was a refuted claim in its comments; all are fixed in `e766f23`/`d6153b8`. The seat that found the lock defect is also why R5's own branch stops short of a lock repair: that is now `· R7`, deliberately left open rather than solved with an unverifiable regeneration.

iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.target: OPEN, and deliberately not fixed with a lock regeneration. History, because it is the instructive part: the row was first closed the same day on a regeneration (`b43234b`) that dropped funasr's dependency tree (99 packages to 85) — and that regeneration was **reverted** in `902879c` after two review seats independently found it resolved `torch 2.14.0` from PyPI plus 18 `nvidia-*`/`cuda-*` packages, which `uv sync` would have installed over the verified `repo.radeon.com` ROCm build on the one host every GPU result comes from. `main`'s `uv.lock` is therefore byte-identical to `1f2dcd0`'s (`sha256 4cf305d6…`) and still stale, which is the honest state: stale-but-CUDA-free beats fixed-but-destructive. The correct fix is a regeneration that keeps torch out of the resolution (a `[tool.uv]` source or override) — see `· R7` for the hazard that fix must avoid. It needs a resolution verified against `repo.radeon.com`, which was impossible when this was found because PyPI and DNS were unreachable from the target host, so it is left for a round that can verify the result instead of guessing one.
iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.tracking: Register row `iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout · R6`. Commit `b43234b` on `feat/20260927-aac-decode-contract`. iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.closure_evidence: State at `d6153b8`: `bilibili-asr-archive/uv.lock` is byte-identical to `main` (`sha256 4cf305d6…`, 99 packages), so its root `asr` extra still reads `asr = [{ name = "funasr" }]` — a package the engine stopped using when it moved to Qwen3-ASR — and it still declares no `accelerate`. `pyproject.toml`'s `[asr]` extra declares transformers/accelerate/soundfile/soxr. So `uv sync --extra asr` installs a closure that does not match the declaration, and `README.md:1015` documents `uv sync` as a supported install path. What is NOT true, and was the error in the earlier closure: that regenerating the lock is a safe fix. It is not, without keeping torch out of the resolution.
iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.closure_note: REOPENED 2026-09-27, and the reopening is the point of this row's history. It was closed earlier the same day on the claim that regenerating the lock fixed it. That claim was wrong: the regeneration was reverted in commit `902879c` after two independent adversarial review seats found it installed a PyPI CUDA torch on the ROCm host, so the lock is stale again and the defect is open. The closure was not merely premature — it asserted a fix that had a destructive side effect, which is the failure mode this whole branch exists to correct. Kept as a reopened row rather than deleted so the record shows the closure that did not hold.

iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.title: **Any lock regeneration for this project silently pulls a PyPI CUDA torch, because `accelerate` requires `torch` with no marker — and `uv sync` would then replace the verified `repo.radeon.com` ROCm build on the one host every GPU result comes from.** `pyproject.toml` deliberately does not declare torch and says so in a NOTE, but a NOTE constrains nothing a resolver reads: `accelerate>=1.0` is in the `[asr]` extra, so a resolution materialises torch and its whole NVIDIA closure.
iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.source: Found 2026-09-27 by two independent adversarial seats on PR #20 (one reviewing ASR runtime code, one reviewing the dependency contract), each reaching it separately and each grading it must-fix. Reproduced by the driving session reading the lock: `torch 2.14.0` with `source = { registry = "https://pypi.org/simple" }` and `files.pythonhosted.org` wheels, plus 18 `nvidia-*`/`cuda-*` packages, against `pyproject.toml`'s own note and `README.md`'s "pip is deliberately told nothing about torch". Base comparison: 0 CUDA packages, no torch.
iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.scope: Any `uv lock` / `uv sync` invocation against this project, and therefore the documented `uv sync` install path. `pip install -e ".[asr]"` is unaffected in the sense that it does not touch the lock, but it has the same resolver behaviour with respect to `accelerate`'s torch.
iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.target: Mitigated, not closed. `b43234b`'s lock was reverted in `902879c`, restoring `main`'s bytes and taking the CUDA closure out of the repository. `pyproject.toml` now carries a WARNING naming the incident, saying the lock is deliberately left unrepaired, that `uv sync --extra asr` is not a working way to get a GPU environment here, and that a future regeneration must keep torch out (a `[tool.uv]` source or override) rather than accepting the resolver's default. Doing that properly needs a resolution against `repo.radeon.com`, which could not be performed when this was found — PyPI and DNS were both unreachable from the target host — so it is left for a round that can verify the result rather than guessed at.
iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout.tracking: Register row `iter-2026-09-qwen3-asr-closeout · R7`. Commits `902879c` (revert), `d6153b8` (the pyproject warning). Related open row: `· R6` (the stale lock itself, reopened because its earlier closure claimed this regeneration as the fix). Disclosed in PR #20. The general lesson — a version omission guarded only by a comment is not guarded at all, because comments are not inputs to a resolver — belongs to the next iteration's compound round, alongside R6's lock-file lesson.

REACHABILITY: fetch_pages has no production caller — `fetch-meta` runs the WBI-signed x/space/wbi/arc/search path (MetadataIngestor + BilibiliApiGateway) and terminates on empty pages only, and the CLI exposes no keyword entry point. 20260926-video-metadata-enrichment.detail: Measured 2026-09-30 against mid 23191782. (1) Rows are trustworthy: every exhaustively paged keyword (爱情/拉康/笛卡尔/恋爱/庶政学/常常/格尔黑/子明未/主义主义) returned only rows whose titles literally contain the keyword, 0 exceptions; a full re-enumeration reproduced the 2026-09-25 1730-row snapshot exactly (missing 0, extra 0), and the 哲学 sweep (ps=30, pn=1..15) served a union identical to the corpus literal set (406 == 406). (2) `total` is a separate, looser upstream quantity: 7 candidate matchers fitted against 56 measured keywords — the best matched only 39/56; `革命者的常态` reports total 27 with 0 rows returned and 0 corpus titles containing all 7 characters; description-indexing is ruled out (BV11p5qzAE6s's desc holds both 爱情 and 革命者的常态, yet `刻意追求性压抑` from the same desc returns 0). The exact upstream matcher stays uncharacterised and is not worth further probing. (3) The 1739-vs-1730 gap is the same mechanism split across the walk: last-page row counts at ps=100/50/30 are 39/39/29, matching 1739's pagination arithmetic exactly (not 1730's 30/20), while interior short pages pn 5,6,7,8,20,24 deficit exactly 9 — the index holds 1739 and 9 rows are dropped when rendering rows. (4) The defect is directional: a `total` above the true count only costs an extra page (caught by the empty-page and no-new-bvid stops), but a `total` below it truncates silently. `total` was never measured below the row count, so no live data was lost — this is a latent-defect fix.

20260927-evidence-dashboard.tracking: PM-confirmed structurally (both gates read on main); the reviewer's end-to-end 1/0 measurement could NOT be reproduced by the PM (three fixture attempts produced invalid bundles both readers correctly flagged) — registered at structural strength, see detail
20260927-evidence-dashboard.detail: Structural fact, confirmed by reading both modules on main@2696711: quality._artifact_paths computes `inferred = not values` and only then offers the inferred candidate families, whereas integrity's raw_candidates (both writer-real raw names) are built unconditionally. Consequence: a row that declares ANY path key never has the two inferred raw names offered to coverage, so an escape at the undeclared raw location is invisible to `coverage --quality` while `verify` reports it. The reviewer measured verify=1/coverage=0 on such a row at both `pre` and `post` (neutral on the §2f diff, and present at base0 in a different form), non-writer-reachable. PM could not reproduce the end-to-end exit split (fixtures attempted were invalid bundles); the structural asymmetry stands on its own. §2f's letter speaks to EXISTENCE, not DECLARATION — so whether the pair must also agree on the declared axis is an open scope question, not settled by §2f. The reviewer attached a candidate patch (qc3-r2-candidate-B-R18.patch) that closes it and passes the touched suites plus the full suite, measured at ~0.56 s -> 2.01 s on 3000 healthy declared rows.

20260926-audio-inventory.title: UNREADABLE-BUT-PRESENT FILE IS COUNTED AS `missing`. `reconcile_audio_inventory` catches OSError from the digest read and increments `missing`, but contract §3.1 defines `missing` as a manifest row that NAMES an audio_path whose FILE IS NOT THERE. A present-but-unreadable file (permissions, I/O error) is therefore reported under a counter whose definition excludes it -- the local-redefinition §3.1 forbids. The PM chose it because the alternatives are worse (no digest means the object cannot be recorded; counting nothing would hide the file entirely), but the choice is unruled. Needs a product ruling: a fifth counter, a stderr warning with no counter, or an explicit §3.1 amendment.

20260926-audio-inventory.title: CONTRACT WORDING, not a code defect. Section 3.1 words `recorded` as "a manifest candidate that had NO audio_objects row and now has one", but the fix round had to decide a case the wording does not cover: a row that EXISTS and does NOT match (a file replaced in place). The implementation counts that as `recorded`, because the run wrote the content afresh -- calling it `already` would assert the "and matched" the same section requires of that counter, and counting it as neither would hide a rewrite. The next unchanged run then reports `already`, which is the convergence F8 asked for.
